rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Gameplay 2.1 Round End 2.2 Hand End 2.3 Game End 3 Variants 3.1 Grumpy Goat Overview Combine cards to make whole numbers e.g. 5-2-8 is 852, and play the highest value combos in order to empty your hand the fastest. Gameplay Each player start with 9 cards. The first player plays 1 card. Following players can play 1 or more cards, or pass. The value of the card(s) played must be greater than what is already on the table. Values of multiple cards are combined in such a way to form a whole number of the highest value possible (e.g. 3 and 4 make 43). You can play the same quantity of cards as previously played, or exactly 1 more. If you play more than one card, they must all be of the same numeral or same suit (e.g. 888 or blue 5-3-1). Once you have played, take one of the cards from the play you just defeated into your hand and discard the rest. If you cannot or do not wish to play, you pass for now, but you still get a turn when it comes back to you again. Round End If all other players pass, you win the round and become the first player. Clear the area. Hand End If you start the round, and all cards in your hand are the same suit or value, you can play your whole hand instead of just one card and end the hand. Otherwise, when a player empties their hand the Hand is over. Everyone gains 1 point per card still in their hand when this is triggered - Be mindful that on the BGA adaptation, you lose points instead of gaining them. Game End Depending on the length of the game, the game ends when a player reaches or exceeds 10/15/20 points. When that happens, the player with the fewest points wins. In the BGA adaptation, the game ends when one player reaches zero points and the player with the most points wins. Variants Grumpy Goat 1 Grumpy Goat is shuffled into the deck. The Grumpy Goat is treated as a 0 of any color. If you have the Grumpy Goat in your hand at the end of a hand, you receive 5 points.

---

I can't imagine any kids who would enjoy this very much.  Much like Hachi Train, there's many turns where you sit there passing, doing literally nothing, while watching the others play a light game. This is one of the reasons I liked Nanatoridori slightly better (everyone's constantly drawing cards), but at least Hachi Train had some rising stakes as the round progresses, and the pressure of being the last one with cards. Tried really hard to push forward to see if something was missed, but nothing could save it : my mouth dropped, and continued to drop, by how random, boring and pointless it was. [Rating: 3/10] Super disappointed with this game. I bought it because I saw people calling it “ scout killer” but not even close. This game has almost no strategy. If you a player is forced to skip because they dont have a higher hand then that person is basically screwed. You will keep on having to skip almost every time until the round is over. I can see why people compare it to scout because of some similarities but this game so dull and boring. My game group does not want to play this again.

[Rating: 3/10] The card play was kind of fun but when half of your turns are just passing, it starts to feel like less and less like an actual game.
